literal: Country, they say, unseeking wealth-having; countries are not, to seek wealth giving country.
translation: A true country is one that possesses wealth without it having to be sought. A land that yields wealth only through hard seeking is no country at all.
modern: முயன்று தேடாமலேயே செல்வத்தை உடைய நாடே சிறந்த நாடு என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவார்கள். மிகவும் முயன்று தேடிய பிறகே செல்வத்தைத் தரும் நாடு சிறந்த நாடாகாது.
explanation: This couplet defines the ideal economic state of a country. A true country is one where wealth and resources are naturally abundant and easily accessible without strenuous searching. If a land requires its people to struggle and search extensively just to find basic wealth, it does not deserve to be called a great country. The contrast between 'நாடா' (without seeking) and 'நாட' (by seeking) emphasizes that prosperity should be effortless for the inhabitants.
